newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Santer hopes enlargement talks will start on time.
newsitem.headline: Santer hopes enlargement talks will start on time.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer said on Monday he hopes accession talks with central and eastern European countries can start as planned in early 1998, but he urged the countries concerned to do their homework.

"Everything will depend on the preparation of the candidates. The better they prepare themselves, the shorter will be the deadline for accession," the Commission said in a statement on Tuesday after Santer met Hungarian President Arpad Goncz.
According to the established timetable talks should start six months after the end of the Intergovernmental Conference on European Union.

Despite recently voiced Commission concerns about the slow pace of the talks Santer said he hoped the IGC would end in the first half of 1997 during the Dutch presidency of the EU, which would allow enlargement talks to start in 1998.
Goncz said he hoped Hungary would be in the first tier of countries to be admitted and suggested the creation of a pre-accession fund to help the process.

The European Commission is currently examining the results of questionnaires submitted by the candidate countries and on the basis of those questionnaires will draw up its opinions on the individual countries' applications.
